answer: Each identity must complete a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings before its Wesolowski proof can be verified; each step depends on the previous result, so GPUs cannot shorten an individual chain through parallel computation. An attacker may run clone chains concurrently, but each clone still incurs the full delay and resource cost, limiting cheap Sybil identities. The mirror, opal, and gale labels do not change this per-identity bottleneck.
